portals.note: Linked from the BCAD homepage. Not opened, and the page does not state whether access is free.

facts.summary: EPA issued the third five-year review for the Gulfco site on August 5, 2026 and determined the site is currently protective in the short term.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, Gulfco Marine Maintenance (site id 0602027)
facts.quote: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) issued the Third Five-Year Review Report on August 5, 2026.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile describes the 40-acre site as located in a primarily undeveloped area in the city of Freeport, with its southeastern edge bordering the Intracoastal Waterway. The page gives no date for this description.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, Gulfco Marine Maintenance (site id 0602027)
facts.quote: The 40-acre Site is located in a primarily undeveloped area in the city of Freeport in Brazoria County, Texas.

gaps: No owner of record was established. The EPA profile does not name the current owner, and the atlas owner is null. Ownership needs a BCAD owner or ID search or a clerk deed search.
No parcel number was matched. The atlas address is a county road (BRAZORIA COUNTY RD 756), and a BCAD search was not run for this site.

The NPL listing date (May 2003 in an EPA document excerpt) was not confirmed on an opened page, so it is not recorded as a fact.
The Brazoria County Clerk search returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. The search was not run, and access terms are unconfirmed.

sites.name: MARINE CORPS COMBAT DEVELOPMENT COMMAND

portals.name: PWC-County Mapper (Prince William County GIS)
portals.note: Opened the application page only. The page lists browser requirements and does not say whether access is free. No parcel query was run for this site, and the installation is a federal reservation rather than a county parcel.

facts.summary: EPA added the Marine Corps Combat Development Command site to the National Priorities List in May 1993. The site covers about 56,000 acres across Prince William, Stafford and Fauquier counties.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, Marine Corps Combat Development Command (site id 0302840)
facts.quote: The Site was added to the Superfund program's National Priorities List (NPL) in May 1993.

facts.summary: The Department of the Navy has the lead role for cleanup. The 2023 five-year review concluded that response actions are in accordance with the EPA-selected remedies. The page gives no date for the lead-role statement.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, Marine Corps Combat Development Command (site id 0302840)
facts.quote: The Department of the Navy has the lead role for cleaning up the Marine Corps Combat Development Command NPL site.

facts.summary: EPA's profile says institutional controls at one operable unit (OU 4) include land use controls, groundwater use restrictions and groundwater monitoring. For OU 19 it says land use control measures are being developed. The page is undated.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, Marine Corps Combat Development Command (site id 0302840)
facts.quote: Institutional controls in place include land use controls, groundwater use restrictions, and groundwater monitoring.

gaps: The atlas point (38.56106, -77.4255) is an installation reference point on a federal reservation of about 56,000 acres, not a county parcel. No county parcel, owner or deed record was searched for this site.
No transfers, liens, permits or tax records were searched. Federal installation land is not expected in county assessment records, but this was not checked against the Prince William assessor.
The EPA profile says a Redevelopment section exists, but its text was not opened.
The EPA profile is undated and cites only a 2023 five-year review. Any later cleanup status was not found.
The atlas owner is null and the record gives no federal agency for the land. The Navy lead is from EPA, not from a land record.
